title: Dock public research/reader projection: rights and review containment ledger
scope: Dock public routes /reader, /reader/compare and /research plus the hub owner of /corpus/reader and /corpus/browse. No application code was changed.
quote_semantics: source.quote must occur verbatim as a substring of the trimmed source line at source.file:source.line

claims.claim: Clearance is an exact token, not any non-empty rights field: only RIGHTS_EXACT_VERSION_CLEARED is treated as cleared.
The shared veto compares the edition rightsStatus to the exact cleared token, so PUBLIC_DOMAIN remains a label and cannot clear text.

source.quote: const isCleared = (edition: Row | null): boolean => nonEmpty(edition?.rightsStatus) === CLEARED

claims.claim: /corpus/reader derives editionCleared from the edition rights before serializing any passage field.
A translation is cleared only when both the edition and the translation row are exactly cleared.
An uncleared translation serializes text:null instead of its wording.
The Arabic object is present only when the edition is cleared and text exists.
The public reader returns state available only for a cleared edition, otherwise rights_blocked.
A blocked reader states that text is withheld and names the edition rights status.

source.quote: message: editionCleared ? null : `Text withheld: edition rights are ${meta.rightsStatus}.`,

claims.claim: The research overview endpoint is ADMIN_ONLY; it is not a public projection of research records.
The research case endpoint, which carries claims and evidence spans, is ADMIN_ONLY.
The research trace endpoint is ADMIN_ONLY.
No endpoint in packages/moonql-research declares requires: 'public'; every declared research endpoint is admin- or auth-gated.
Even the admin-only research case projection labels itself ENGINEERING_ONLY rather than approved for publication.
The research case projection hard-codes humanReviewed false; it is not a human review or a D08 approval.
The research release verdict type fixes publicationAvailable to false, so no research release path can claim publication today.
Dock's public /research page renders only the localized withholding alert and no research records.
The /research page test forbids readResearchRegistry, ResearchExplorer, serverClient and model reads on the public page.
A blocked response carries a machine-readable placeholder in place of text, not an empty success.
The blocked placeholder is a fixed non-source string that cannot carry verse wording.
The negative matrix asserts that an uncleared edition serializes no Arabic object for five citation variants.

source.quote: assert.equal(data.arabic, null, `${citation} (${fixture.status}) must serialize no arabic object`)

claims.claim: A research case with a rights-unknown source is still rights_blocked when its address is read through /corpus/reader.
The absent path returns no Arabic object rather than an empty or invented verse.
The absent path returns no citation text and no candidates.
The Dock reader derives a withheld flag from the upstream rights_blocked state.
The Dock reader renders Arabic text only when the withheld flag is false, even if a projection returns bytes.
The Dock reader renders translation text only when the row has text and the withheld flag is false.
A blocked Dock reader states the denial in words instead of rendering a silent empty panel.
The public compare page body is a heading plus one withholding alert; it renders no source text.
The compare page metadata states that source text is shown only after an approved public projection is available.

source.quote: description: 'Compare only source text available through an approved public projection.',

claims.claim: The compare-page test forbids the former inline edition data, citation helper, self-asserted clearance badge and text payload.
The compare-page test forbids the former Indonesian-translation marker and the Sahih International label in the public page source.
Raw corpus_passages rows, which hold arabicText, are ADMIN_FULL rather than ADMIN_WRITE.
Raw corpus_translations rows, which hold translationText, are ADMIN_FULL rather than ADMIN_WRITE.
ADMIN_FULL gates list and get, not only writes.
The REST list route applies the model ACL as a preHandler guard.
An undefined ACL rule would be public, which is why the ADMIN_FULL declaration on text-bearing models matters.
The denial matrix asserts 401 for anonymous raw reads of corpus_passages and corpus_translations.

claims.claim: Anonymous raw research model lists and details return 401 and carry no synthetic or cleared bytes.

source.quote: assert.equal(res.statusCode, 401, `${path} must deny anonymous raw Research reads: ${why}`)

claims.claim: Anonymous calls to every declared research endpoint return 401 and carry no bytes.
The admin-only research payload reports nothing as published, released or approved for publication.
/corpus/browse is public but its response body contains neither arabicText nor translationText and no cleared bytes.

claims.claim: The browse export flag is true only for an exactly cleared context edition.
Dock reads passage text only through the hub projection /corpus/reader, not through an ORM model.
Dock reads the rail metadata only through /corpus/browse.
